paper: XPlainVerse: A Million-Scale Benchmark for Explainable Deepfake Detection
reviewed_scope: Official arXiv v1, all 50 PDF pages including appendices H/I, metrics and limitations; reference positions [1]–[70].
full_text_findings: About 1M images: 470K authentic from five sources and 530K synthetic/manipulated from twelve systems; Edit-Check retains about 265K of roughly 609K initial fake candidates. Twelve annotators wrote explanations for 2,000 manipulated images. Ten-image overlap set was independently annotated by five people; authors report EntityScore=.50 and EvidenceScore=.44 as agreement. Ten institutionally recruited adults participated in a seven-stage human evaluation. Complex explanation ratings: composite 3.79/5, grounding 3.82, specificity 3.96, completeness 3.78, convincingness 3.79, unsupported claims 2.43 (lower better). Simple explanations: 3.94/5 composite, ease 4.11. EntityScore/EvidenceScore use offline Qwen3.5-4B for extraction and bidirectional semantic coverage of prediction/reference explanation text.
reliability_evidence: Direct evidence for reference-grounded entity/evidence coverage, limited human agreement on a small overlap set, subjective quality ratings, readability/preferences, and narrative ID/OOD grounding analysis.
construct_limitations: Qwen semantic matching against fallible reference text is not an independently adjudicated visual-fact test; the same judge is used to extract and score. The 10×5 overlap and custom semantic agreement metrics do not establish conventional chance-corrected inter-rater reliability. The human study does not test detector-assisted decision accuracy, calibrated trust, or appropriate reliance. No model-decision causal faithfulness, necessity/sufficiency, or explanation sanity/perturbation validity is established. Small institutional participant pool limits generalization. PDF Table 5 text encoding prevented reliable transcription of some numeric cells.
